analysis.title: JPM Market Intel Morning Update, Nov 13, 2026
key_insights: Market is described as coil-sprung to go higher, with the pain trade seen as up. Yesterday the rally extended despite higher yields, NVDA gapping down about 15% and AI headwinds. Institutional participation was light.
Retail were aggressive dip-buyers in NVDA, about a 9 standard deviation move in NVDA buying volume by 10am (10.1z per the FINS desk) and more than 5 standard deviation buying in Mag7.
2Y yield is +33.7bp and 10Y +26.7bp week to date, which makes the equity resilience on reduced participation surprising. 10Y was at 5.123% in the morning update.

PPI is due at 8:30am ET. Feroli expects headline PPI +0.6% MoM (6.8% YoY), the fastest YoY pace of the current cycle, and core PPI +0.4% MoM (5.1% YoY), which would exceed April's peak. PPI is seen as a read-through to PCE and the Dec to 27Q1 Fed reaction function.

Feroli sees core goods and core services both strong, citing Flash PMI and ISM surveys that point to AI capex, energy, shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz (written 'SoH') and tariffs as inflation sources.

Fedspeak is hawkish: Daly says inflation pressure is up, AI is fueling price pressures, and she is comfortable with a September hike with further tightening needed. Goolsbee sees old-fashioned demand overheating. Hammack says the Fed is not behind the curve but a larger move could be needed if it falls behind.

FINS desk (Taylor Barry): tape is shrugging off NVDA. Multi-manager platforms have deleveraged heavily over recent weeks, so lower grosses and tighter nets make the pain trade higher. Positioning Intel: short exposure fell from +2.7z to +0.4z over a month while long exposure rose only from -0.8z to -0.3z, so the move was mostly short covering. NA positioning went from -0.7z to +0.2z.

TMT desk (Heavey): NVDA supply largely dissipated after heavy pre-market and open selling. SMH turned positive, read as money reallocating within AI rather than leaving it. AVGO and AMD seen as the biggest beneficiaries of a weaker NVDA, and money is rotating into GOOGL on its TPU program. Mgmt at GOOGL has a long-only meeting next week on Search concerns.

NVDA leadership/financing risk: Jensen Huang's departure is a stated risk, with interim CEO Colette Kress reportedly opposed to some of his financing deals, including a proposed $250B credit backstop for OpenAI that was split in two, with about $100B guaranteed so far. NVDA CDS hit record highs on reports Huang may be removed.

Equities desk (Kussin): value traded would be the lowest in two weeks excluding $80B of NVDA traded. Institutional activity is subdued and hedge funds are tentative to add risk given recent performance. Next Thursday is seen as a hopeful clearing event, and the pain trade is higher.

Consumer desk (Barton): no evidence of broad rotation of real money into consumer; long demand is selective and quality-skewed (KO, HD, PG, WMT). HD and LOW are emerging as popular longs ahead of earnings. WMT setup is muted on valuation after a >20% move since October. TGT has gone from the most crowded HF long to increasingly a short, with a roughly $160 downside against an $11 bull case and a multiple above 16x people don't want to underwrite. TJX/BURL positioning is depressed, ROST is the crowded long with shorts emerging.

JPM Credit (Spear) is Underweight NVDA bonds, expecting continued spread weakness during the leadership transition and legal/regulatory fallout. NVDA has only about $35bn of debt, so the larger issue is AI ecosystem financing and circularity. Existing commitments are not assumed to change, but new deals could take longer or cost more.

Spear sees export control implications as potentially more consequential than the leadership change, and expects a tougher oversight environment when the new Congress takes office in January after last week's blue wave.

JPM Equity (Harlan Sur) removes NVDA's 'China + Other' shipments (about 8% of F1H27 revenue) from FY28 revenue estimates, cutting FY28 EPS about 10%. Applying about 15x gives a new $215 Dec 2027 price target. He expects NVDA to keep AI leadership with roadmaps defined for the next 2-3 years.

US Market Intel is Tactically Bullish. It reads the Nov 10 CPI-driven selloff as a reset of yields higher toward economic growth (about 3.4% in 26Q3). The Tech washout looks at or near completion, with some risk of another Semis decline. It suggests broad Tech and US Memory and Semis via options, and a barbell of Tech plus Cyclicals, with Cyclicals better played via European names for lower positioning and valuation.

Recession fears from the AI selloff are called inaccurate. JPM's recession basket is +14.9% since Sep 30 while SPX -1.7%, NDX -8.8%, SOXX -22.7% and DRAM -32.7%. A decline in AI capex is unlikely to cause recession since it added little to jobs, and consumers hold large cash balances with a near full-employment labor market.

Feroli: nonresidential construction, contractors and heavy and civil engineering jobs were up 165,000 over the year, only 0.1% of total employment. Professional, scientific and technical services jobs rose 33,000, a sign that the feared AI job loss is still far off.
Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 on $365 EPS at 21.9x, implying 8.4% upside from Friday's close.

Dubravko's trade ideas: long 12M momentum vs short 3M momentum (essentially Tech vs Energy/Defensives); Low Vol less compelling after moving from 0%ile to 25%ile, with Healthcare, Utilities and Staples the best low vol options; AI upstream attractive after the positioning flush; consumer cyclicals challenged by affordability, with longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail vs Energy. Mortgage rates need to approach 6.0% for housing inflows.

Dubravko attributes the pullback to deleveraging after record leverage in AI plays, with liquidity drying from late June. October was the largest single-month unwind for Long Momentum (about -11%, roughly 6 standard deviations), with Momentum L/S down about 40% from peak. Equity multiples have compressed about 4x since January, AI companies about 35% since May (Semis 52%, hyperscalers 14%, Memory 60%, Processing Units 50%).

How much selling is left per Dubravko: Momentum crowding reset from 100%ile to 76%ile; levered ETF sales of about $60bn Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday; CTAs flipped net short with maybe $50bn left to sell; dealer net gamma imbalance at 12%ile; $1.2T of announced buybacks as support; QQQ RSI below 30, which has averaged about a 4% rally over five trading days.
Dubravko's catalysts: Middle East developments, megacap IPOs, next month's ERCOT meeting (AI capex implications), and the December Fed meeting. He sees midterms as a clearing event.

AI capex sensitivity: every $100B of added capex translates to about $9 of S&P 500 EPS (about 2.5% earnings growth) in 2027. Mid-range capex of about $1.5T would add about $18 vs consensus, or 4-5% to 2027 EPS growth. JPM credit analysts expect hyperscalers can fund 2027 capex absent credit shocks, with funding needing more equity participation.

Morning snapshot: SPX +0.2%, NDX -0.0%, RTY +0.1%, WTI -94bps at $87.91, gold $3,894, silver $49.93, VIX 18.35. DXY set a new 52-week high. IEA points to oil surpluses for the first time since the US-Iran conflict began. Pre-market Mag7 were higher except MSFT (outage issues), while Memory, Semis and Software were lower.
